column1: # Marker-text audit: every numbered "Deciphering the Icon" marker read against the picture
# under its own circle, at full size, with crops where the detail is small.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The reading audit (icon_reading_audit.tsv) finished 2026-09-21 and
# examined MARKER TEXT on only the 48 icons it touched that day; roughly one marker in three
# on those was wrong. The other 65 icons — the rows marked checked-2026-08-21b and
# checked-2026-08-22 there — had their PROSE read against the picture and their MARKER TEXTS
# never examined by anyone. This file is that sweep. 65 icons, 347 markers.
# A ROW HERE MEANS NOTHING UNLESS hotspots.js / hotspots3.js SAYS WHAT THE NOTE SAYS. The
# reading audit's 28 fixed-2026-08-22 rows recorded corrections that were never applied to
# the source, and the reader shipped the wrong text for a month. Every `fixed` row below was
# written AFTER the edit landed and AFTER grepping the old wording out of the source.
# One row per MARKER, not per icon — per-icon rows are how 47 bad marker texts hid behind 65

column5: note   (verdict: holds | fixed-DATE)

he does not recline and his hand is not raised: he sits upright on a cushioned seat and his right hand is down at his knee, fingers reaching toward the woman. Prose in hotspots2.js said 'reclines' too and was fixed with it
position right, but her hair is bound under a white cloth — nothing is wiped with it. Added what is there: face turned up, hands at his bare foot
the vase is there and upright, two-handled and white, standing on the pavement below the couch; the prose called it 'emptied on the floor', which the picture does not show
a press of eight or nine unhaloed heads at the right, two hands legible in gesture over the table
one footed bowl at the centre of the cloth, with round loaves, long loaves and green sprigs about it
the robe is not plain — a dark red mantle over a gold-shot green brocade sleeve; hand flat on the table edge is right, and the column that sets him apart is now named
'seated' cannot be seen — the table cuts him at the waist; he is at the centre behind it in a yellow hood and veil, both hands down on the cloth
not a heap: the coins lie spread flat in one layer under both his hands
caps and hoods, not turbans; one elder seated in orange in front and a beardless young man in blue among them

column3: The canopy and the drawn curtain
column5: a red velum swagged between the flanking buildings and gathered at both columns, over a gabled central portico

column3: Christ at the head of the table
column5: cruciform halo confirmed at full crop, but no bread is painted on this table: the blessing hand is at his breast, the left hand reaches over the cloth
ὁ δεῖπνος left of the hanging lamp, ὁ μυστικός right of it — both read at full crop
'the only beardless face among the twelve' is false — at least two more beardless apostles on the right side; and he is bowed forward at the Lord's side, not leaning back
an arm comes in from the right and the fingers are over the rim of the central basin
not bread and a cup: a footed basin at the centre with a dark flask, two small cups and knives — the icon's own prose reading said so and the marker contradicted it
upper left, reclining, the one gold halo in the panel (abraded); his hand is over the bowed disciple at his breast
bowed small and close under the Lord's chin, head almost on the table

column3: The hand stretched to the dish
column5: the reach is more exact than the text said: the hand comes down INTO a small footed cup on the cloth, which is the dipping itself
two footed cups, a lidded vessel and triangular wedges all lie in full view on the tilted top
counted twice at full crop: TWELVE apostles, not eleven — seven behind the table and five seated in front with their backs half turned
a gabled building at each upper corner with a plain wall between them
read at full crop: ΗΑΡΝΗCΙC ΤȢ ΠΕΤΡȢ, lunate sigmas and an ou-ligature — the denial of Peter
the company at the fire is two soldiers in scale armour and helmets and a young man in blue, not servants, and Peter sits apart across the flames from them
a girl in red in the doorway with her right hand up, pointing at him
'another maid names him again' is not in the picture — the fresco paints one maid and repeats Peter instead
he is not sitting with his face in his hands: he is bent double over a green column with his face buried in his arms

not a wall above him: the flat roof of a small white building beside him, and the bird's head is thrown back with the beak open, crowing. Prose in hotspots2.js called it 'a little pillared roof' and said 'two moments' where the wall paints three; fixed with it

column3: Christ at prayer on the rock
column5: upper left, haloed, bowed deep over the rock
four figures of Christ on this wall, not three prayers: two bowed, one upright at the top centre, one turned back to the sleepers — which is what the icon's own prose reading already said
haloed, head inclined, right hand out and down toward the sleepers
not 'the three' — about a dozen figures fill the whole foot of the wall, the eight told to sit here as well as the three taken farther on
the rock is ochre and pale olive where the light falls; only the crags along the top are near-black. 'grey and black' described no part of it
the titulus is longer than the marker gave: Η ΠΡΟΣΕΥΧΗ ΤΟΥ ΧΥ, the Prayer of Christ. ΙΣ ΧΣ beside each figure confirmed
far left, kneeling on the rock, both hands stretched out to the right
three kneeling figures of Christ across the left two-thirds of the wall, a fourth standing at the right
standing over the sleepers in dark red, right hand out and down
both hands are open toward the Lord, not one, and he is the grey-haired one
about eleven heads heaped at the foot of the rock, wrapped and inert

the fresco paints Luke's angel — a small winged haloed figure high in the dark sky — and no marker or reading had ever named it. Added to the prose; a marker there would clamp to 9% and land on Christ's halo
…LATE 7 OR… / …TIS IN TEM… legible at full crop, with a Tironian 7 for ET; the left half of the band is too worn to read in this photograph

column3: The angel out of the gold
column5: it does not come head-first: it flies in level from the left with its hand stretched out to meet Christ's, and carries no cup
kneeling on the hill, both hands lifted toward the angel
he stands upright, not bending, and holds a closed scroll in his left hand — the scroll was in no text
heaped across the middle and the whole lower left of the panel
ΗΠΡΟΔΟCΙΑ read across the top
green tunic, one arm across the body and the other hand on the far shoulder, face to face, no halo
cruciform halo confirmed at full crop, still, one hand down

MISPLACED as well as wrong: the sword at the left belongs to the arresting party, not to a disciple. Peter and Malchus are at the LOWER RIGHT — marker moved from 48%/27% to 76%/85% and the text rewritten to what is painted there
there is also an axe and a white gabled lantern with the flame inside it, held up on a staff, against a black sky pricked with stars
the man laying hands on him wears no armour — a beardless youth in a plain red tunic with a dagger at his belt; the armoured soldier stands behind him
·RADITIO· at the left of the band and DOMI[NI] at the right, both read at full crop
his face is set straight forward, NOT turned to the man kissing him; cruciform halo confirmed
one arm round him, not both — the other hand reaching across the Lord belongs to someone else in the press
bottom left, Peter grips the servant's head and holds the blade at his ear, the servant down on the ground
a lantern AND a hanging lamp on poles, and two long axes and a knobbed club among the spears

he wears no cuirass and no armour — a pointed cap and a mantle over a white tunic. The 'one Roman in armour, and the state behind the council' was not in the picture; label changed to 'The man at the right edge'
the halo is deep orange-red and the cross in it is faint, not the clean cruciform the text implied; and his hands are not visible at all, so 'one hand at his side' was invented
leans in from the left, face against the Lord's cheek, arm across him
spears, two axe-heads and a curved blade raised in a line across the top
right, and better than it said: the monogram ΙΣ ΧΣ is lettered either side of the lantern's pole over the Lord's head

nobody is struck in this fresco — no servant on the ground, no ear. A man in red holds a sword raised over his head, and nothing identifies him as a disciple. Label changed to 'The raised sword at the left'
there are no helmets and no armour anywhere in the panel; every head is bare. Label changed to 'The bare heads of the crowd'
Ο Χ͞C ΚΡΙΝΟΜΕΝΟC ΥΠΟ ΑΝΝΑ ΚΑΙ ΚΑΙΑΦΑ read at full crop; the marker expands the nomen sacrum, which is fair
and better than the text said — both hands have the tunic pulled apart at the breast and the pale undergarment shows through
right, and his raised open hand toward the prisoner was left unsaid
haloed, standing before the seated judges
no book and no lectern: a white sheet of imitation script and a black inkwell on a low yellow table
no cuirass and no spear in his hands — a green belted tunic, laced red leggings, arms folded, a shaft leaning behind him
his hand is not lifted toward the accused: the front of his robe is painted as a mass of torn strips with his hand at the tear — Gračanica paints the rending, the verdict, not the question
a man in red between the seat and the prisoner with his arm thrown out toward Christ
standing, haloed, head bowed, wrapped in the mantle with no hands showing
helmeted, in tunic and cape with a sword at his side, his hand at Christ's arm
a group of pale-robed men behind the guard at the right edge
right, and now says what is there: the cock stands on the crown of the arch with lettering either side of it on the black ground
ΥΠΕCΤΡΕΨΕ ΤΑ ΤΡΙΑΚΟΝΤΑ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΑ read across the top
red mantle over a teal tunic, bent over the table with his hand down among the coins
no cloth — a bare yellow table-top, and beside the coins an open written scroll, a reed pen and a black inkwell that no text mentioned. Label changed to 'The silver on the table'
the crowned one seated at the end of the table and a second seated beyond him, neither rising, a press of heads behind
right, and the fresco letters his name ΙȢΔΑС beside his head, and dresses him in the same red mantle as at the table — neither was said

the buildings are not identified as the temple by anything in the picture: a pink enclosure wall and a green red-roofed building with its door open, and a small figure in a red hood leaning over the parapet to watch
one tree with a spreading crown and nothing else growing in the field
the cord runs from the branch down behind the head to the neck; the face is fully painted, thrown back, mouth open
pale rock in steps, no building and no other figure
only the right hand is legible, open and half curled; the left is lost in the folds, so 'the hands' was one hand too many
no feet are in the photograph at all — the wall curves away below the hem. Label changed to 'Where the picture ends'
the fresco writes ΑΠΟΝΗΨΙС with an eta, not ΑΠΟΝΙΨΙΣ, and the ΙΣ ΧΣ is in the sky above the halo, not beside it
crowned, on a raised seat, both hands out over the basin
and the same soldier in lamellar armour holds the basin under his hands; the water is a thin painted arc
cruciform halo, head bowed, both hands held loose before him, unbound
the head is uncovered and the hair bound up — Orthodox painting veils its women, so the figure cannot simply be called Pilate's wife; the marker now says what is there and why readers take it for her
a press of bearded elders from the right, the front one with his hand raised
'hands crossed in front of him' cannot be seen on this darkened panel; one hand comes forward at the waist. The point that stands is that nothing binds him
three helmets, and spear shafts above them, which the text left out
crowned, seated on the wooden throne in a gold-banded robe, arm out toward the accused
one white headcloth and one gold cap; the two in front are bare-headed, so 'turbans and caps' overstated it
a beardless servant behind the throne-back, bent forward, a dark oval vessel held at his chest
a wide platform in flat red and pale bands under the seat
stripped but for a white loincloth, bound at the pillar, head turned aside
not 'at the front' — both arms go right round the pillar and the wrists are tied on the far side, a red cord across the wood
white tunic, arm up, the thongs in his fist and the lash curving away above him
mirrors him from the other side, arm up, lash in the air
right, and the board carries a red Slavonic title nobody had read: the surviving half is …СТОЛПА, 'at the pillar'
not crenellated — a flat wall with a band of painted triangles and a stepped cornice; no door, which was the point and stands
the long curve of the body along the wood, head fallen toward his Mother
ΙС ΧС in red on the upper limb, read at full crop
two small winged figures flying in from either side above the arms, hands wrapped in their mantles
her hand is not at her face: the right hand is held open toward her Son and the left is at her breast
opposite her in a pale olive himation, hand to his cheek
busts round all four sides, and a crowned man and a crowned woman side by side along the foot
arms wide along the bar, head sunk toward his right
the board is there but nearly effaced — four letters divided by points, the Greek ΙΝΒΙ; the marker implied it was legible
she is the MIDDLE of three and is being held up under the arms; the woman nearest the cross is another, in blue. Her maphorion is rose, not red
opposite the Mother, hand to his face
right, and he is HALOED — the marker never said so, and it is the thing that makes him St Longinus rather than a soldier
a black cave with a skull AND two long crossed bones, not a skull alone
a battlemented brick wall across the whole ground behind the cross
the long sagging curve, arms out along the bar
Ο ΒΑCΙΛΥC left of the body and ΤΗC ΔΟΞΗC right of it, read at full crop
ΜΙΧΑΗΛ lettered at the top left and Ο ΓΑΒΡΙΗΛ at the top right, both flying in, the right one's hand under his mantle
her hand is not at her breast: one fist is at her chin and the other hand is open toward the cross, and her face is turned up to him. Gold star on the shoulder
opposite her, head bowed, hand to his face
red stars scattered thickly over the gold either side of the body

'carried in procession on a pole' is not established anywhere in the record; what the museum does say is three layers of paint, the earliest ninth-century — the cross, the body and the two angels. Marker now says that

column3: The Mother's face against her Son's
column5: she has his head in her lap and her cheek against his
exactly — bent double, the Lord's hand in both of his, pressed to his cheek
stretched the width of the picture on a white cloth woven with gold crosses; the wound is visible on the hand

column3: Joseph of Arimathea at the feet
column5: grey-bearded, stooping over the feet at the right
a cylindrical vessel standing at the bottom left edge
the hill is pale ochre, not green — the green is the ground band along the bottom; and it is not bare: the abbreviated holy names are painted on it beside the haloes
the cross stands behind the group with the title board still nailed to it and Χ͞С lettered beside it
cheek pressed to his face, his head in her arms at the left end of the slab
the slab is red, the body wrapped from the waist in white

column3: The woman with her arms thrown up
column5: the mantle is salmon-orange over dark blue-green, not red, and her hair has fallen loose — worth having, since it is what marks her out
bent over the body at its side
he is not bringing it down — it leans against his shoulder while he holds a rung and props his cheek on the other hand
right, and the painter's signature runs along the same band and nobody had read it: ΧΕΙΡ ΕΜΜΑΝȢΗΛ … ΛΑΜΠΑΡΔȢ
the two haloes are there, set inside one another, but both faces are rubbed away — the marker described features that no longer exist on the panel
'wrapped from the waist, the wounds shown' cannot be read: the paint at the loins is rubbed to the ground. The body is bare, head left, feet right

column3: The empty cross with its title
column5: the cross stands behind with the small board still on it

column3: The disciple bending to the body
column5: a haloed figure in red bent over the body near the head
he holds the Lord's legs with both hands, one at each ankle — not the shroud
the ladder is a rail with rungs held up behind his shoulder, and his face has darkened past reading
a rank of haloed women behind the Mother
right, and it is a blue slab ruled into panels that fills the cave mouth
one hand, not both: his right hand is flat on the slab with a small dark seal in it and his left is raised. The headgear is a domed cap, not a turban
'a patterned robe' is ribbed scale armour — he has a spear in his hand and a red shield at his feet, which is what makes him the watch
the spear is held upright past his shoulder, not across his knees, and his shield lies on the ground in front of him
a white-bearded man in dark blue standing between them, watching
FIVE haloed figures, not four, and the first is a grey-bearded man — they are not all women. Slavonic lettering above them
now quotes it: ГРОБЪ ГОСПОДЕНЬ, read at full crop
six helmeted heads, not four — five faces still legible, all with the eyes shut
scale painted over the whole group, scale by scale
the shields are large OVALS painted with radiating stripes, not round shields with bosses
the claim was right and the marker was in the wrong place — the open hand with the shaft across it is at 42%/61%, not 85%/55%. Moved and relabelled

column3: The edge of the tomb above
column5: the photograph shows only pink-red folds and a corner of white along the top; the sarcophagus base and the white angel are not in it. The fact about what is painted above at Mileševa is kept, as a fact about the church rather than about this frame

the loss is real and the apostles with open books are there, but the Theotokos and the Forerunner cannot be identified in what survives and their raised hands are not visible; marker now says a standing figure survives either side of the loss. Ranks of winged angels behind the benches added
it cannot run 'from under the throne' — the throne is the part that is destroyed; it runs from under the place where the throne was
confirmed at full crop, and sharpened: a black mass crowded with small heads, a pale-robed soul on his knees, a gold arc behind both
the whole left half in orderly rows
right, and now says what they look like: dark blue squares packed with pale faces, red squares with figures in flame, each with a red Greek line over it
the bands are there but the words cannot be read at any available resolution — the marker asserted the text. It now says what is visible and what such bands carry
centre of the panel, enthroned with the Child on her lap, the tree growing round her
right, and the painter signed the ground beside him — ΧΕΙΡ ΒΙΚΤΩΡΟΣ · ΑΧΟΔ ·, the hand of Victor, 1674 in Greek numerals — which nobody had read
crowned figures in the upper branches

the scrolls do not carry prophecies: each carries a NAME from Matthew's list — ΑΒΡΑΑΜ, ΡΟΒΟΑΜ, ΑΒΙΑ were read at full crop. 'The words by which he foretold the Child' was the standard Tree of Jesse read onto a panel that does something else
a pale disc at the top left with one long ray running down behind the house
not a band: four lines standing in the gold, and abbreviated — MAGI MUNERA OFFERUT DNO IESU XPO. The marker had silently expanded it
counted three at full crop, and they are vessels shaped like jewelled crowns, which is worth saying
'the dress of foreigners' is not what is painted — tunics and cloaks, and only the eldest has his head covered, in a white wrap
seated, the Child on her knee over a white cloth, her hand at his back
the hand is open with the fingers spread, reaching — it is not the sign of blessing the marker claimed
riding with the Child, the ass moving right toward the town

column3: The Child held in her arms
column5: carried in front of her, doing nothing
he carries no bundle — he leads the ass by the rein, grey-bearded and barefoot; the bundle is on the youth's staff

column3: The young man with the staff
column5: he is at the TAIL of the beast, not at its head — the ass faces the town and he strides along behind it
right, and a crowned figure steps out of the open door with a bundle and something gilt — the personified city, and no text had mentioned it
no crown on him and no enthroned king anywhere in the panel — two bearded men under the colonnade and a written placard on the column. The marker asserted a seated king it could not show
the middle of the panel is swords up and children taken
they fill the lower half, holding and pleading

column3: The angels carrying the children up
column5: blue-robed angels on a cloud at the upper right with small naked children in their arms

column3: The slain at the foot of the icon
column5: bodies laid along the bottom edge

column3: Ο ΩΝ in the arms of the halo
column5: the three letters read in the cross arms
ΙС at the top left, Χ͞С at the top centre
checked letter by letter: ΔΕΥΤΕ ΠΡΟС ΜΕ ΠΑΝΤΕС ΟΙ ΚΟΠΙΩΝΤΕС ΚΑΙ ΠΕΦΟΡΤΙСΜΕΝΟΙ ΚΑΓΩ ΑΝΑΠΑΥСΩ ΥΜΑС, ΑΡΑΤΕ ΤΟΝ ΖΥΓΟΝ ΜΕ… ΜΑΘΕΤΕ ΑΠ ΕΜΟΥ — Matthew 11:28–29, as the marker said
two fingers extended, thumb to the ring finger, at full crop
right, and the fresco letters him Ο ΠΡΟΔΡΟΜΟΣ, which was not said; 'burnt by the sun' dropped as a reading of the skin tone rather than an observation
the Deesis claim is now anchored in the picture: the scroll in his other hand opens ΔΕΞΑΙ ΔΕΗΣΙΝ, receive the petition. No text had mentioned that he holds a scroll at all
standing in the dark water, which rises round him like a grave
the marker hedged — 'the axe OFTEN lies at the root of a tree'. It is in this panel, at the root of the small tree below him, and now the marker says so
four angels, two behind two, and the cloths they carry are what covers their hands — both details were missing
the ray ends in a small pale DOVE under a scalloped segment of heaven, and the marker had left out the Spirit in a marker about the Trinity
right, and now quotes the mosaic as it is lettered: SI FILI DI ES DIC VT LAPIDES ISTI PANE FIA
the reply begins SCRIPTUM EST, which is the marker's own point about reading Scripture to the devil, and he holds a closed scroll while he says it — neither was in the text
loose stones lie between them in the middle of the field

column3: The devil as a winged figure
column5: dark, thin, black-winged with white outlines, hands out toward Christ
bare rock across the bottom of the field
right, and now carries what the tier-b decision of 2026-09-20d rests on: the Greek line across the top is about an appearing (ΕΜΦΑΝΙCΑС … ΤΟΙС ΥΠ ΑΥΤ ΓΕΝΟΜΕΝΟΙС), not the words of Matthew 28
'indistinguishable in glory' is contradicted by the panel — four distinct faces, a red book and a white scroll among them
'turned outward, already leaving the frame' is false: every apostle on both sides faces inward toward Christ
Ο Χ͞С ΙΩΜΕΝΟС ΤΟΥС ΑСΘΕΝΟΥΝΤΑС ΑΠΟ ΠΟΙΚΙΛΩΝ ΝΟСΩΝ read across the top
the hand touches nobody — it stops short of the man reaching back, with bare wall between them; and a scroll is closed in his other hand
a close rank of heads at his shoulder
long sticks held and leaned on through the right of the crowd
their legs are stretched OUT, not drawn under, and blotched with sores; two wear wide straw hats
three registers of three, the nine scenes the tier-c note of 2026-09-20d counted
the dark red bands do carry rows of pale Slavonic lettering, divided into one panel per scene

column3: The crowds in the open country
column5: half the compartments are architecture — porticoes and interiors — so 'out of doors' described only part of the panel

column3: A burial in the lowest register
column5: right, and the body wound in a white shroud beside the opened ground is the thing that makes it a burial; the marker had only the digging
no figure in the panel is large
POTES ME MUNDARE across the top

the touch is NOT painted: a hand's breadth of bare gold lies between Christ's hand and the leper. The icon's own prose reading said so and the marker contradicted it — 'the icon makes the touch the centre of the picture'
spotted from face to feet
he leans on a long stick, standing apart at the right
the dark scaled mass of the hill fills the upper left
a close group of heads behind his shoulder
Ο Χ͞С ΙΩΜΕΝΟС ΤΟΝ ΥΙΟΝ ΤΟΥ ΕΚΑΤΟΝΤΑΡΧȢ — the son, as the marker says
right, and better: a low painted wall stands between him and the centurion, which is the distance the miracle is worked across
scale corselet, gold bands, crested helmet
right hand up palm out, left hand out flat and open
he is NOT lying: upright behind a red coverlet, fair-haired in a green tunic, his face turned up toward Christ
IHS LIBERAT SOCRV SIMONIS A MAGNIS FEBRIBVS, in two lines across the top

'reaching out and taking hold' is wrong — a band of bare gold lies between his hand and hers. This is the same mosaic the Mark gotcha of 2026-09-20 already recorded, and Matthew's marker had gone on saying the opposite
already sitting up on the bed, turned to him
the white coverlet fills the lower right
the arcaded front and the arched door behind them
there is no doorway: five faces pressed into the left edge against a painted wall. Label changed to 'The disciples crowded at the edge'
it can be read, and now is: Х͞Ъ ВЪ КОРАБИ ПОВЕЛѢВАЮТЬ ВѢТРȢ ДА ОУМЛЪЧИТЬ — Christ in the ship commands the wind to be still

column3: Christ standing to rebuke the sea
column5: he stands at the LEFT END of the boat, not the middle, with his hand raised toward the waves rather than out over the water, and a scroll in the other hand
right, and the disciple leaning in with an outstretched arm to wake him was left out — it is the moment the marker's own Chrysostom quotation is about
working the ropes and looking up at once
the rigging crosses the whole upper half
hard scrolling ridges, filling the bottom of the field
Ο Χ͞С ΙΩΜΕΝΟС ΤΟΝ ΔΑΙΜΟΝΩΝΤΑ ΚΩΦΟΝ across the top

column3: The hand of Christ at his face
column5: not 'head and mouth' and not two hands: one hand, with the fingers laid on his EAR — which is the point of κωφός, and the marker had missed its own argument. Label changed
'brought and held by others' is not in the picture — he stands alone on his feet, hand at his own breast

column3: The man arguing at the right
column5: a man at the right with his hand up in argument
close rank of heads at his shoulder
Ο Χ͞С ΙΩΜΕΝΟС ΤΟΝ ΠΑΡΑΛΥΤΟΝ across the top
he speaks from where he stands, hand raised, and touches nobody in this fresco either
and it is a framed bedstead with turned posts, carried across the shoulders with both hands on the frame
no claim about the picture to check; the verse is Matthew 9:6
figures still lying on their beds under the arcade at the right
close group behind his shoulder

this is the fresco whose five-bay arcade and round well-head make it John 5. Recorded in HANDOFF as the owner's call; no marker or reading was changed here, and none of the six markers asserts anything false about the architecture
plain gold, no cross, abraded along the top
the reed is in his right hand
the codex is CLOSED, not open — gold tooled covers, red spine with raised bands, page-block showing. Nothing is written on it
white-bearded and old, not the publican at the toll booth

read at full crop: IHS FILIAM IAYRI PRINCIPIS SYNAGE IN DOMO EIVS SVSCITAT. The mosaic NAMES Jairus, and Matthew does not — he is 'a certain ruler' in this Gospel; the name is Mark's and Luke's. Now said
and it is his LEFT hand, down at the edge of the bed, with her hand closed in it — the two hands really do meet in this mosaic
'already lifting her head' is far short of it: she sits bolt upright with her arm stretched out and her hand in his
mourners crowded at the right, and one of them holds a round timbrel — the minstrels are painted
